refusing to auto-apply 50 pending schema migrations to a shared server database (v16 -> v66): migrating would lock out every co-resident bd client still on the old schema (#5920)

  This database is served to multiple clients (dolt sql-server /
  proxied-server mode). Applying schema migrations promotes the schema
  version for EVERY client at once: bd clients still running an older
  version will refuse this database until they are upgraded.

  To migrate (explicit consent):
    1. Upgrade bd on every client of this server first (or accept that
       older clients refuse until they are upgraded).
    2. Then run, once, from a workspace already set up against this
       server:
        bd migrate schema
        (bd migrate schema --global for the shared global database;
        BD_ALLOW_REMOTE_MIGRATE=1 bd <cmd> in scripted/CI use)

  Read commands keep working against the current schema in the meantime;
  writes stay refused until the schema is migrated.

  If the migration then reports dirty tables, that working set has to be
  committed first — see the recovery the dirty-table error names; do not
  re-run this command in a loop.

  join and migrate in one step once every client is upgraded:
